title: What training do you need for a security license in NSW?
description: NSW security license classes, the Security Licence Course units for each Class 1 subclass, first aid every three years, Class 2 entry rules and renewal.
shortAnswer: In New South Wales, most security operatives need a Class 1 license from the Security Licensing and Enforcement Directorate (SLED) of the NSW Police Force. Applicants for every Class 1 subclass except 1E must pass a pre-enrolment assessment and complete the NSW Security Licence Course with a SLED Approved Organisation, built on CPP20218 Certificate II in Security Operations. A current first aid certificate is also required and must be renewed every three years.
keyTakeaways: SLED administers the Security Industry Act 1997 (NSW). Class 1 has six subclasses (1A to 1F) and Class 2 has five (2A to 2E); a person can hold more than one subclass.
Only training from a SLED Approved Organisation counts for a Class 1 application, and it starts with the SLED Pre-Enrolment Assessment, which includes a language, literacy and numeracy test.
Class 1A and 1C need HLTAID011 Provide First Aid; 1B, 1D and 1F need HLTAID014 Provide Advanced First Aid. Either must have been issued within three years and kept current while licensed.
Bodyguard, cash-in-transit, guard dog and armed guard subclasses each need extra CPPSEC units on top of the Certificate II, and armed guards then complete Security Firearms Training.
A license can be renewed from eight weeks before expiry and up to 90 days after it. After 90 days the person must apply again and meet the current course requirements.

sections.heading: Who regulates security licensing in NSW?

blocks.text: The Security Licensing and Enforcement Directorate (SLED) of the NSW Police Force regulates the security industry in New South Wales. According to [SLED's own description](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/online_services/sled/about_sled), it administers and enforces the Security Industry Act 1997 and its regulation, decides who is granted a license, and audits licensees and training providers.

Training sits at the center of that model. SLED has a dedicated Training Regulation team whose enforcement officers visit Registered Training Organisations to check that training and assessment follow the NSW Security Licence Course Conditions of Approval. SLED's privacy collection notice issued in December 2026 names the current regulation as the Security Industry Regulation 2026. Significant amendments to the Act, including a restructure of the Class 1 subclasses, commenced on 1 June 2023.

sections.heading: What security license classes exist in NSW?

blocks.text: NSW issues operative licenses in two classes, plus Master licenses for businesses. [Class 1](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/online_services/sled/security_licences/class_1_licences) covers frontline operational roles and [Class 2](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/online_services/sled/security_licences/class_2_licences) covers specialist and advisory roles. Each class is divided into subclasses, and the training required depends on the subclass.

sections.heading: What does the NSW Security Licence Course require for Class 1?

blocks.text: Every Class 1 applicant except 1E must complete three things before applying. SLED's [training requirements page](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/online_services/sled/security_licences/security_training/security_training_requirements) lists them as the SLED Pre-Enrolment Assessment (including a language, literacy and numeracy test), a first aid certificate issued within the past three years by a Registered Training Organisation, and the current approved mandatory units of CPP20218 Certificate II in Security Operations.

SLED's [course structure document](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0008/278684/Competency_Requirements_for_Class_1_Licences_Dec_2024.pdf) (December 2024) groups the 1A course into four clusters: Security Industry Fundamentals; Patrol, Monitor and Screen; Protect Self and Others; and Manage Behaviour of Others. The 13 units include CPPSEC2106 (basic defensive techniques), CPPSEC2111 (managing intoxicated persons) and CPPSEC2112 (removing persons from premises), which is why the 1A license also covers crowd control.

The higher subclasses add units at Certificate III level, and the pre-enrolment assessment for 1B, 1C, 1D and 1F is set at Certificate III level. Entry to those courses requires either CPP20218 or a current Class 1 license other than 1E. Once a 1F license is granted, a condition imposed under section 23E of the Act requires the holder to complete Security Firearms Training (CPPSEC3114 with either the revolver or the semi-automatic pistol unit) and to apply to the Firearms Registry for a Category H Provisional Pistol Licence.

blocks.title: Primary text: SLED
blocks.text: "Only training qualifications obtained through SLED-Approved Organisations are acceptable for Class 1 licence applications."

sections.heading: How often must NSW security training be refreshed?

blocks.text: NSW has no general refresher course for Class 1 licensees, but first aid must be renewed every three years for as long as the license is held. SLED's [frequently asked questions](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/online_services/sled/security_licences/frequently_asked_questions) also place a duty on Master licensees to ensure that every Class 1 operative they provide, other than 1E, holds a current first aid certificate.

The license itself is renewed through Service NSW. SLED's [renewal page](https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/online_services/sled/security_licences/renew) allows renewal from eight weeks before expiry and up to 90 days after it, with late fees. The holder is unlicensed from the expiry date until the renewal is processed. After the 90 days pass, the person must lodge a new application with evidence that they meet the current security license course requirements, so lapsed holders can be sent back to training if the course has changed since they qualified.

SLED's fee table lists one, three and five year terms. Choosing the term is therefore also a decision about how often the renewal checkpoint falls, and it should be lined up with the three year first aid cycle so the two dates do not drift apart.

sections.heading: What happens if licensees breach their conditions?

blocks.text: Breaches can lead to fines and to suspension or revocation of the license. SLED's Class 1 page lists maximum fines of $5,500 for carrying out security activity without a Class 1 or Class 2 license and for failing to wear the license on the front of outer clothing above the waist, and $11,000 or six months imprisonment for offenses such as selling or lending a license.

Operating conditions also create recordkeeping duties: Class 1 licensees must be provided by a Master licensee, must fill out sign-on registers before and after each shift, and must notify SLED of changed particulars within 14 days. Breaching an additional condition imposed by SLED can attract up to $11,000 and six months imprisonment for an individual or $22,000 for a corporation.

sections.heading: What should a Master licensee's training records show?

blocks.text: A Master licensee's records should prove, for each operative on each shift, the subclass held, the qualification behind it and a current first aid certificate. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats the NSW license as an external credential and maps site-specific post orders, such as screening and ejection procedures, to assessable outcomes that sit on top of it. A security provider can then show which operatives were assessed on which version of each site procedure, as well as holding the right subclass. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Do monitoring center operators need training for a NSW security license?
faqs.a: No formal training is required for the Class 1E Monitoring Centre Operator subclass. SLED lists 1E, 2B and 2C as subclasses that do not require formal training. Applicants still have to meet the age, residency, criminal history and fit and proper person requirements that apply to every Class 1 license.

faqs.q: Does a Master license need security training in NSW?
faqs.a: SLED states that no formal training is needed to apply for a Master license. The business does, however, carry obligations for the operatives it provides, including ensuring that each Class 1 operative other than 1E holds a current first aid certificate and holds the subclass required for the work.

faqs.q: Can a NSW security license be renewed after it expires?
faqs.a: Yes, for up to 90 days after the expiry date, with late fees, but the holder is unlicensed until the renewal is processed. After 90 days the license cannot be renewed and the person must apply again, including evidence that they meet the current security license course training requirements.

faqs.q: Are older first aid units still accepted by SLED?
faqs.a: SLED says it will only accept HLTAID003 and HLTAID006 qualifications that were completed before 30 June 2022. Any first aid certificate must also have been issued within the previous three years, so in practice new applicants and renewing holders will usually present HLTAID011 or HLTAID014.

factCheck.claim: Class 1 has six subclasses: 1A Security Officer, 1B Bodyguard, 1C Cash-in-Transit Guard, 1D Guard Dog Handler, 1E Monitoring Centre Operator, 1F Armed Guard; a person can hold more than one.

Class 1 applicants except 1E must complete the SLED Pre-Enrolment Assessment including an LLN test, a first aid certificate issued within three years (HLTAID011 for 1A and 1C, HLTAID014 for 1B, 1D, 1F), and the CPP20218 mandatory units; first aid must be renewed every three years; only SLED Approved Organisation training accepted; 1E, 2B and 2C need no formal training.

Additional units: 1B CPPSEC3122 and 3123; 1C CPPSEC3118, 3119, 3120; 1D CPPSEC3112 and 3113; 1F CPPSEC3101, 3102, 3103 followed by Security Firearms Training and a Category H Provisional Pistol Licence. 2A requires CPP41519 and five years experience; 2D requires a TAE Certificate IV and three years experience; 2E requires CPP30619.

Class 1A course structure has four clusters and 13 CPPSEC2xxx units; Certificate III level pre-enrolment assessment for 1B, 1C, 1D, 1F; Security Firearms Training is a condition imposed under section 23E of the Security Industry Act 1997.
Renewal online up to eight weeks before expiry; 90 days after expiry to renew; after 90 days a new application with evidence of current course requirements is needed.

Maximum fines: $5,500 for security activity without a Class 1 or 2 licence and for not wearing the licence; $11,000 and/or six months jail for selling or lending a licence; additional conditions breach up to $22,000 corporation or $11,000 and six months individual; sign-on registers each shift; notify change of particulars within 14 days; fee table lists 1, 3 and 5 year terms.

Master licence holders must ensure Class 1 operatives they provide, except 1E, hold a current first aid certificate; no training needed for a Master licence; HLTAID003 and HLTAID006 only accepted if completed before 30 June 2022.
SLED administers the Security Industry Act 1997; Training Regulation team audits RTOs against the NSW Security Licence Course Conditions of Approval; significant amendments commenced 1 June 2023.
SLED's December 2026 privacy collection notice names the Security Industry Act 1997 and the Security Industry Regulation 2026 as the governing instruments.
